c-le-point.label: A point lies on a line when it satisfies the equation
c-le-point.summary: Put the point's x and y into the equation. If both sides agree, the point is on the line.

q-le-point.label: Substitute a point into a line
q-le-point.summary: Find an unknown in the equation, or pick the option point that lies on the line.

c-le-system.label: Two or three lines drawn together
c-le-system.summary: Where two lines cross is the point satisfying both equations; three lines taken in pairs enclose a triangle whose area can be read from the crossing points.

q-le-system.label: Where lines meet, and the triangle they enclose
q-le-system.summary: Solve a pair of equations for their crossing point, or find the area of the triangle three lines form.

formulas.text: Point (p, q) is on ax + by = c  ⇔  a·p + b·q = c
formulas.note: For y = mx + c put y = q and x = p and solve for the unknown.

formulas.text: Solve two linear equations by elimination or substitution to find their one crossing point. x = k and y = m are a vertical and a horizontal line, crossing at (k, m).
formulas.note: Lines like x = 4 and y = 3 are often two sides of a triangle already — their crossing point is a vertex and the two legs can be read straight off.

q-le-point.cue: 'The line … passes through (…)' with one unknown, or 'which point lies on the line?'
q-le-point.standard: Replace x and y by the point's coordinates and solve the one equation left.
q-le-point.fast: For options, test the point with the smallest numbers first. 3x + 2y = 12: (2, 3) gives 6 + 6 = 12 straight away.
q-le-point.eliminate: Check the parity or a unit digit: 3x + 2y = 12 is even and 2y is even, so 3x must be even, so x must be even. That removes (1, 6) and (1, 4) at once.
traps: Subtracting 7 but forgetting to divide by x (13 − 7 = 6, not 3).
Testing only one option and stopping before checking that the others fail.

q-le-system.cue: 'The lines … intersect at the point' or 'the area of the triangle formed by the graphs of …'.
q-le-system.standard: Solve any two of the equations simultaneously to get each crossing point, then use those points (or two of the lines as legs) to find the area.
q-le-system.fast: If two of the three lines are x = k and y = m, they are already a vertical and a horizontal leg of the triangle — the area is just half their lengths' product.
q-le-system.eliminate: Check a candidate crossing point in both original equations before using it further.
traps: Solving the wrong pair of equations for a given vertex.
Forgetting the ½ in the triangle-area formula.
Mixing up which two lines give the two legs of a right triangle.

pyqs.text: The line 3x + 2y = 12 passes through which of the following points?
pyqs.trick: 3x + 2y = 12 is even and 2y is even, so x must be even. Only (2, 3) and (4, 1) have an even x; (4, 1) gives 14.

pyqs.text: The graph of the linear equation y = x passes through the point:
solution: Any point on y = x has equal coordinates.
(1, 1): 1 = 1. True. None of the other three points have matching coordinates.
pyqs.trick: On y = x the two coordinates are simply equal — scan the options for a matching pair.

pyqs.text: The area (in sq. units) of the triangle formed by the graphs of the equations x = 4, y = 3 and 3x + 4y = 12 is:
solution: x = 4 and 3x + 4y = 12 meet at (4, 0); y = 3 and 3x + 4y = 12 meet at (0, 3).
The triangle (4,3), (4,0), (0,3) is right-angled, with legs 3 (along x = 4) and 4 (along y = 3): area = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6.
pyqs.trick: x = 4 and y = 3 are already two of the triangle's sides (vertical and horizontal), so its legs are just read off directly.
